title: WHSmith Travel Essentials Store — Manchester Airport Terminal 2
description: Appointed as architect and Principal Designer (Building Regulations), we took WHSmith's new Manchester Airport Terminal 2 store from concept through to detailed design — leading a dedicated team of four, navigating stringent landlord approvals, building regulations, and delivering a distinctive sense-of-place retail environment within one of the UK's most ambitious airport transformation programmes.
content: When one of the UK's most ambitious airport transformation programmes called for retail fit-outs that could match the ambition of a £1.3 billion terminal, we were appointed as architect and principal designer to deliver the new WHSmith Travel Essentials Store at Manchester Airport Terminal 2 — taking the project from initial concept all the way through to detailed design and construction.

Our project lead headed an in-house team of four, managing the full project from our offices and maintaining close oversight of every stage of the design process. This hands-on, studio-led approach ensured consistency, quality, and clear communication across all workstreams from inception through to delivery on site.

The entire project was delivered in Revit, enabling a fully coordinated Building Information Model throughout. This allowed us to produce detailed 3D realisations of the design — invaluable both for client and landlord approval presentations — whilst facilitating robust clash detection across disciplines. Working in a federated model environment alongside the structural and MEP designers, we were able to identify and resolve coordination issues well ahead of construction, reducing risk on site and ensuring a smoother, more efficient delivery programme.

Our role was comprehensive and exacting. As principal designer, we led the building regulations process end-to-end, navigating the stringent technical and compliance requirements inherent to a live airport environment. Simultaneously, we managed the landlord approvals process in full alignment with Manchester Airports Group's new Terminal 2 fit-out standard — one of the most demanding retail design frameworks in UK aviation, developed to ensure every unit contributes to a genuinely world-class passenger experience.

From the outset, our design approach was rooted in a strong sense of place. The interior draws on Manchester's industrial heritage and creative identity, with the honeycomb lighting feature becoming a signature element of the scheme — an eye-catching focal point that speaks to the city's craft and character. Exposed material finishes, bold graphics, and considered contemporary lighting work in concert to create a retail environment that feels distinctly Mancunian, yet entirely at home within a premium international terminal setting.

Delivering retail design within a major airport transformation requires more than technical competency — it demands an understanding of landlord strategy, passenger flow, brand standards, and programme pressures all at once. We navigated each of these with precision, ensuring the project was delivered on time, on standard, and to a quality that contributed meaningfully to the wider Terminal 2 experience.
The result is a store that has already drawn national industry recognition as part of WHSmith's expansion across the North — a scheme we are proud to have been a pivotal part of delivering

title: Grindsmith Coffee's First Artisan Airport Coffee Concept, Manchester Airport Terminal 2
description: Appointed as architect and Principal Designer (Building Regulations), we delivered Grindsmith's first ever artisan airport coffee concept at Manchester Airport Terminal 2, leading a team of four from concept through to detailed design. Working fully in Revit, we navigated stringent landlord approvals aligned to the new terminal fit-out standard, delivering a distinctive sense-of-place unit that brings one of Manchester's most beloved independent coffee brands to a global audience.
content: When WHSmith partnered with Manchester-born artisan coffee brand Grindsmith to launch their first ever airport coffee concept, we were appointed as architect and principal designer to make it happen delivering the unit from initial concept through to full detailed design within the demanding environment of Manchester Airport's brand new £1.3 billion Terminal 2.

Our project lead headed an in-house team of four, managing the full project from our offices with hands-on oversight across every stage of the design process. This studio-led approach ensured design integrity, programme discipline, and clear coordination from the earliest sketch through to construction on site.

The entire project was delivered in Revit, producing a fully coordinated Building Information Model throughout. This enabled detailed 3D realisations of the design critical for both client sign-off and landlord approval presentations whilst facilitating robust clash detection across all disciplines.

Working within a federated model environment alongside the structural and MEP designers, we resolved coordination issues well ahead of construction, reducing on-site risk and supporting a smooth, efficient delivery programme.

As principal designer, we led the building regulations process in full, navigating the technical and compliance requirements of a live, operational airport environment. Alongside this, we managed the landlord approvals process in strict alignment with Manchester Airports Group's new Terminal 2 fit-out standard — ensuring every design decision met the exacting requirements of one of the most tightly controlled retail environments in UK aviation.

The design itself was crafted to carry genuine sense of place. Grindsmith is a proudly Mancunian brand, and the unit needed to reflect that identity within a world-class terminal setting. The result is a space that feels both local and premium — a post-security destination where passengers can enjoy barista-made coffee and a breakfast and brunch-led menu before their flight, in a space that speaks authentically to the city it calls home.

Located post-security and before duty free, the Grindsmith coffee shop sits adjacent to the new WHSmith travel essentials store Moodie Davitt Report — two complementary units we delivered concurrently, creating a cohesive retail and hospitality offer that contributes meaningfully to the Terminal 2 passenger experience.

Bringing an independent, city-born coffee brand into a major international airport — on time, on standard, and through one of the most rigorous approvals processes in UK retail — is no small undertaking. We are proud to have been a pivotal part of giving Grindsmith its platform on the world stage.

title: InMotion Electronics Store - Copenhagen Airport
description: Appointed as architect and lead designer, we delivered the new InMotion electronics store at Copenhagen Airport, one of Scandinavia's busiest international gateways. Working from our UK studio with a team of four, we produced the full detailed design in Revit and coordinated closely with an in-country technical architect to ensure all statutory and landlord requirements were satisfied to the correct standard for this high-profile European travel retail location.
content: Copenhagen Airport is the largest and busiest airport in the Nordic region, serving close to 30 million passengers in 2024 Wikipedia and operating as a major international hub connecting Northern Europe with the rest of the world. Delivering a retail fit-out in this environment demands precision, rigorous coordination, and a thorough understanding of how to operate across international borders with multiple design and statutory stakeholders. That is exactly what we brought to the InMotion electronics store at CPH.

Our team of four led the project from our UK studio, taking the design from concept through to a fully resolved detailed design package. As with all our international projects, the entire scheme was produced in Revit, giving us a coordinated Building Information Model throughout the process. This enabled us to generate detailed 3D realisations of the design for client and landlord sign-off, as well as carrying out thorough clash detection across all building disciplines. Working within a federated model environment alongside structural and MEP designers, we were able to identify and resolve coordination issues in the design stage, well before work began on site.

On international projects of this nature, statutory approvals are the responsibility of an appointed in-country technical architect. Our role was to produce a detailed design of the standard and quality required, then work closely with that technical architect to ensure the correct packages were prepared and submitted to fully satisfy both local building regulations and the airport landlord's fit-out requirements. This process demands clear documentation, tight design discipline, and effective cross-border communication, all of which our studio managed from end to end.

InMotion is WHSmith's specialist airport electronics retail brand, operating over 120 stores with more than 20 years of experience in airport electronics retail WH Smith, carrying leading brands including Apple, Bose, Samsung and Sony. The Copenhagen store sits within one of Europe's most commercially active airport environments, where passenger expectations and landlord standards are both exceptionally high. Delivering a unit that meets the InMotion brand standard while satisfying the requirements of a major international airport landlord is a challenge that calls for both design quality and technical rigour.

We provided both. The result is a store that serves the millions of passengers passing through Copenhagen Airport each year, representing InMotion's continued expansion across European travel retail and our continued delivery of high-quality airport retail design across international locations.
